sentence: The pores you can see are little doorways, into narrow tunnels called hair follicles.
claim: Visible skin pores are the openings of hair follicles (the pilosebaceous unit).
note: [SOURCE-READ via search summary] Pilosebaceous unit = follicle + attached sebaceous gland; the follicle opens at the skin surface. Sources do not address pore appearance directly: wording is a plain-language version. A person opens the source; dermatologist sign-off required.

sentence: Even where you can't see one… a fine hair is usually growing inside.
claim: Most follicles, including on the face, produce fine vellus hair.
note: [SOURCE-READ via search summary] Vellus hair is fine, soft, largely unpigmented; facial 'peach fuzz'. 'Usually' kept deliberately; palms/soles have no follicles, which the film does not claim. A person opens the source; dermatologist sign-off required.

sentence: Partway down sits a small oil gland.
claim: Sebaceous glands are attached to hair follicles and empty into the upper follicle.
note: [SOURCE-READ via search summary] Glands are holocrine, closely associated with follicles (esp. face), secreting into the follicular canal. A person opens the source; dermatologist sign-off required.

sentence: Its cells do something strange. Each one slowly fills with oil… until the whole cell breaks down and becomes oil.
claim: Sebocytes accumulate lipid as they mature, then disintegrate and release their contents as sebum (holocrine secretion).
note: [SOURCE-READ via search summary] Holocrine = the whole cell is the secretion; the gland cycle takes about a week (not stated on screen). A person opens the source; dermatologist sign-off required.

sentence: That oil is called sebum. It glides up along the hair, and spreads over your skin in a thin, soft coat.
claim: Sebum travels up the follicle and spreads across the skin surface, forming most of its surface lipids.
note: [SOURCE-READ via search summary] Sebum is about 90% of surface lipids in adolescents and adults. 'Glides up along the hair' is a visual simplification; the film does not name a mechanism. A person opens the source; dermatologist sign-off required.

sentence: Tiny microbes live in there too, quietly feeding on that oil.
claim: Cutibacterium acnes and other microbes live in the follicle and use sebum lipids (via lipases) as a food source.
note: [SOURCE-READ via search summary] C. acnes is a commensal of the anaerobic part of the follicle; its lipases degrade sebum lipids. Strain/disease links are less settled and NOT claimed in the film. A person opens the source; dermatologist sign-off required.

claim: Follicle openings can become blocked by sebum and shed cells (the starting point of a comedone), which leads into the next episode.
note: [SOURCE-READ via search summary] Teaser only, no explanation on screen; sources for the full mechanism belong to ep16 (pimple). Needs a dedicated source check. A person opens the source; dermatologist sign-off required.
